summary: Economy layer (records 14, 15, 40-44). Read all 71 goods, 4,300 cell goods (record 40; 689 land/sea cells carry a good), 505 burgs' production/treasury/product, 16 markets with their 71-good stock and prices (record 42), 8,058 deals (record 43: 6,235 market->burg, 1,759 burg->market, 64 market->market) and the kingdom's taxes (salesTax 0.17, pollTax 0.18, treasury 9,568). AGREES (no change): the sale-tithe of 17% equals the history's tithe on every sale (VI-0086/0131/0154); Ceann leathan's market (II-0068), Ros fhionn's salt fair (III-0147), Cathair dhomhain's toll charter (II-0138), Ros bheag's trade court (II-0160), Baile Mòr dhomhain as the hill market (V-0198), Baile Mòr fhionn as the plain's market and Cathair fhada's merchants of the Fèill (gazetteer); silver in the eastern hills, gold near Baile dhìreach, the Baile ghorm salt cell (I-0100), olives (III-0073), honey, grain, cattle, sheep, fish, hemp/rope, dyes, clay/pottery, wool, timber, venison; all 16 market centres have plaza=1 and no history market town lacks a plaza. CONFLICTS (map edited to the history): Slaves -> Seal-oil and Elephants -> Oxen (goods foreign to the island's history), Coal -> Charcoal (the history closes every coal working by 2022-25), no silver at Muileann chiar, no copper at Àth fhiadhaich, salt at only one cell although the history gives Àth bheag, Seann Warr and Caol ìseal salt-pans, no paper at Muileann chaol/Tobar dhìreach, no rope at Seann Tarr/Baile ghlas, no cloth at Doire ghlas/Baile chiar (22 map edits). MISSING FROM THE HISTORY (written in): the whole present-day economy (new appendix G_trade.md), market rights for 11 market centres that had none, amber, marble, wine, tobacco, whaling, glass, scent, the coin-blank trade (27 villages craft Coins), the regiments' arms trade (arms are the top good sold back to towns in every market), the head-tax and the 17% sale-tithe (24 annals events); 58 gazetteer history additions (all 16 market centres and the big producers).

map_edits.why: No age of the annals knows slavery on Rodos; the five shore cells and Ceann mhòr's export of this good to Ceann leathan match the seal-oil trade of the north-west (II-0198). Renaming the good keeps its cells, burg production and deals consistent.
goes with the rename to Seal-oil
goes with the rename to Seal-oil

Rodos is a cold northern island with no elephants in any age; the good (supply/military beast, 2 cells on the Caol leathan plain, exported to Ceann leathan) matches the ox-teams and drovers of the annals (III-0098, VI-0023/0024).
goes with the rename to Oxen

The annals close every coal working before the present: the western seams flooded and capped in 2022 (VI-0122: no coal dug outside the Board's works), the Sloc Mòr upper galleries closed 2025 (VI-0144), 'the coal is all but gone' (VI-0157). The map's 24 hill cells and four producing towns (Àth fhada 174, Baile chrom 187, Cathair naomh 192, Dùn dhubh 471) plus the good's own recipe (1.5 wood -> 1) are charcoal-burning, which the annals know (III-0199, V-0026).
Silver on the cell of Muileann chiar (burg 419), the island's silver seam in every age (II-0016, IV-0173, V-0137 'richer at depth'); the town produces none.
Muileann chiar mines silver (see record 40 edit).
Copper on the cell of Àth fhiadhaich (burg 12), the copper-town of V-0206; the town produces none.
Àth fhiadhaich's copper workings (V-0206).

Salt on the cell of Àth bheag (burg 492), whose pans 'supply the whole eastern seaboard' from 1961 (V-0124, V-0157, VI-0023, VI-0100); the map has one Salt cell on the whole island and Àth bheag makes clay.
Àth bheag's raw good becomes salt (see record 40 edit).
Salt on the cell of Seann Warr (burg 64), the salt-pans the humans came back for twice (IV-0019) and whose salt the carters of Baile gheal hauled all through the Age of Strangers (IV-0105).
Seann Warr's salt-pans.

The gazetteer's present-day Caol ìseal is 'salt pans of the low strait'; its cell keeps Iron (the map's iron and field-gun forges are written into the history), and the pans are added as a second raw good.
Tobar dhìreach's paper-mill, which makes nearly every page of the royal chronicle (V-0077); the town makes arms and tools on the map.
Muileann chaol, the first paper mill on Rodos (III-0218) and the library's copyists and binders (V-0076).
Muileann chaol's copyists and binders (V-0076).
The rope-makers of Seann Tarr, chartered 1982 (V-0182, VI-0017 'the rope-walk at Seann Tarr').
Baile ghlas: gazetteer 'rope-walks and sail-lofts'; the town makes no rope on the map.
The wool mills of Doire ghlas (V-0202, V-0191, VI-0062); the town makes only tools on the map.
The chartered weavers of Baile chiar (V-0065, V-0191).

map_edit_notes: record 40 is the comma-separated cell-good array (index = cell id). 'op': 'append' means push 'value' onto the burg's production array (record 15, index = burg id). Renames in record 41 keep good ids, so cells, production, market stocks and deals stay consistent. Do not run the app's Regenerate Goods/Markets afterwards: it would redraw every good and deal at random. Burg product/treasury and market stocks are not recomputed by these edits; the differences are a few units.

event.title: Amber from the Hawk bay
event.body: Lumps of amber gathered from the wrack on the strands of the Hawk bay are found drilled for stringing in the middens below Seann Skell. A bead of the same amber lies in the oldest ground of the ford gathering, carried there the length of the island.

event.title: The market under the Hall
event.body: A market is held under the walls of the Hall at Dùn ìseal on the quarter days, when the households of the eastern hills come up with their dues. Hides, venison, charcoal, honey and the silver of Muileann chiar change hands there, weighed on the new weights. The Keepers allow no coal to be sold on their ground, and none is.

event.title: The market at the fords of Baile Mòr dhomhain
event.body: The lords of the deep river set a market at Baile Mòr dhomhain, where the carriers' road from the south meets the paths down from the hill pastures. Cattle, sheep, horses, hides and the white stone of the hills are sold at the fords on the day after each new moon, and the lords take one fleece in forty from the sellers.

event.title: The fleece-measure of Baile Mòr fhionn
event.body: The lords of the western plain hold a market at Baile Mòr fhionn and make the fleece of a grown ewe its measure. Grain, wine, cattle and the horses of the plain are all priced in fleeces. The silver rings of Muileann chiar are taken there too, but reckoned in wool.

event.title: The market charter of Cathair fhada
event.body: Queen Sìleas grants Cathair fhada a market each week on its ridge and a tally-house for the south, the first market right cut on paired sticks. The long city's merchants carry the honey, hemp, wax and pots of the south to the capital, and they begin to go to the harvest fair at Muileann òg as one company.

event.title: The market inside the new gate
event.body: Seann Skell on the Hawk bay is walled, and a market is chartered inside the new landward gate. Amber, whale-oil, honey and the sheep of the northern moors are sold there, and the amber-workers of the bay agree to sell no rough amber outside the walls.

event.title: The feast-market at Seann Tarr
event.body: The crowds that come to the ancestor shrine at Seann Tarr for the great feasts begin to hold a market on the three feast days. Its chief goods are honey, beeswax for the shrine lights and the dyes of Baile fhiadhaich. The wax lights of Seann Tarr are soon burned at ancestor shrines along the whole north-eastern coast.

event.title: The market of the eastern road
event.body: Baile Mòr dhìreach, the citadel on the eastern straight road, is given a market for the east coast. The fish and sail-cloth of the coast towns meet the furs, hides and dyes of the hills there, and the dyers of Baile Mòr ruadh sell their colours nowhere else.

event.title: The strand-market at Àth fhionn
event.body: Àth fhionn, the ford town where the coast road crosses the clear river, holds a market on the strand for the north coast. Fish, the flesh and oil of stranded whales, wool and barley are sold there, and the fishers of the north coast stop carrying their catch to Inis mhòr.

event.title: The market above the mill-race
event.body: The hill-lords of Baile ghorm hold a market at Cnoc bhàn, above the long mill-race of Muileann fhada, for the farms of the south-east. Grain, clay and honey are its common goods. Its rare good is pearls, which the women of the shore take from the mussel beds in the shallows and which are sold in no other market.

event.title: The market-court stays at Ros fhionn
event.body: The salt-masters take their ships to Caol gharbh but leave their market-court on the headland at Ros fhionn, where the weights and the tally-sticks are kept. The farms and forges of the north-eastern hills go on bringing their goods to it, and the town keeps its market after it has lost its harbour.

event.title: White stone from Baile Mòr dhomhain
event.body: Masons from Ceann leathan buy a veined white stone from the hills above Baile Mòr dhomhain for the new front of their temple. The quarry is worked from this time on, and its marble goes south by the carriers' road to every town that can pay for it.

event.title: The dark wine of Àth shean
event.body: The growers on the slopes above Àth shean press blaeberry and bramble into a dark wine that keeps a year in the cask. It is sold along the eastern road, and the road-houses serve it as black wine.

event.title: Tobacco on the concession farms
event.body: Human farmers of the northern concession plant tobacco on the sheltered slopes behind Ceann mhòr and sell the dried leaf to the Company's ships. It is the one crop the humans brought that is still grown on Rodos.

event.title: Whale-boats out of Àth fhionn
event.body: Human fishermen of the concession teach the boats of Àth fhionn to hunt whales with the hand-lance instead of waiting for them to strand. The oil is sold to the Company for its lamps, and whale-boats go out from the north coast every summer after this.

event.title: The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach
event.body: Peter Voss, a glazier left behind when his Company contract ended, builds a glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach and melts the white sand of Cuan ruadh with charcoal from the hills. It is the first glass made on Rodos. His Ròdaich apprentices take the craft to the towns of the capital shore within a generation.

event.title: The market of Ceann mhòr
event.body: When the shires are drawn, the Tuathaich of Ceann mhòr are given a market right for the north-west coast. Its court sits in the harbour store whose locks the fishermen had broken. Fish, whale-oil, seal-oil, amber, dyes and the tobacco of the concession farms are sold there.

event.title: The head-tax
event.body: The council lays a head-tax on every household, reckoned on the grown persons the census counted. It is set at eighteen in the hundred of the Crown's reckoned wage and is collected by the maoir of the shires with the harbour dues.

event.title: The cattle-market at Muileann fhionn
event.body: Muileann fhionn, the mill-town the humans built to guard the northern landing, takes a market right for the north-western interior. The Tuathaich drovers bring their cattle and sheep to it, and the droves go south from it to Ceann leathan and the south-eastern farms. It becomes the largest cattle-market on the island.

event.title: The scent-makers of Seann Vell
event.body: The glass-houses of the capital shore begin to make small flasks, and the women of Seann Vell sell in them the waters they distil from bog-myrtle, meadowsweet and heather honey. Within a few years scent is sold in every market town, and the towns of the western plain take up the trade.

event.title: The eastern blank-houses
event.body: With more silver coming up from Muileann chiar than the mint at Cathair dhearg can refine, the Crown contracts the villages of the eastern hills to refine the guild's bar, and the gold washed from the stream below Baile dhìreach, into blanks for the realm-coin. The mint strikes them. The villages are paid by weight.

event.title: The market charter of Caol ruadh
event.body: Caol ruadh, whose harbour victualled the garrisons and the second fleet through the war, is given a market right for the southern strait. It is the sixteenth market town and the last to be chartered.

event.title: The sale-tithe
event.body: The Treasury fixes the tithe carried forward from the war at seventeen in the hundred and lays it on every sale a town makes into its market and on every sale between markets, whether of dubhan or of anything else. A clerk of the Treasury is set in each of the sixteen market towns to take it and to keep the market roll.

event.title: The regiments' arms contracts
event.body: The forges of Àth naomh in the west and Caol ìseal on the north coast, which smelt the bog-iron of their districts, take the Crown's contract for the regiments' small arms and field-guns. The forge-towns of the old vein country follow. Arms become the dearest common goods in every market of the kingdom.

gazetteer_edit.new: It is the market town of the gulf and the old vein country, fifty-two towns in all, and the dearest market on Rodos. Its own trade is in cheese and salted food, and its yards build seagoing hulls.
gazetteer_edit.name: Ceann leathan

gazetteer_edit.new: It is the market town of the capital shore, and its own workshops bind books and put up salted food for the ships.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cathair dhomhain

gazetteer_edit.new: The salt trade that built the bridge has gone, but the market-court the salt-masters set up stayed on the headland, and the town is still the market of fifty-three towns of the north-eastern hills, the widest reach of any market. Its yards on the river build barges and hulls, and it makes cheese for the hill towns.
gazetteer_edit.name: Ros fhionn

gazetteer_edit.new: It is the market town of the Hawk bay and the north-central coast. Amber from the bay's strands is the one good it sells to other markets, and its yards build seagoing hulls.
gazetteer_edit.name: Seann Skell

gazetteer_edit.new: It is the market town of the west coast, and its own trade is in books, boots and salted food.
gazetteer_edit.name: Ros bheag

gazetteer_edit.new: It is the market town of the north-eastern coast, whose market began at the shrine's feasts. Honey from its heather and wax for the shrine lights are its own goods, with cheese and books, and its rope-makers are a chartered guild.
gazetteer_edit.name: Seann Tarr

gazetteer_edit.new: It is the market town of the eastern hills and plain, and the market under the Hall is older than the kingdom. The silver, gold and copper of its hills pass through it as blanks for the mint, and the town salts venison and binds books.
gazetteer_edit.name: Dùn ìseal

gazetteer_edit.new: It is the market town of the northern hills and the second cattle-market of the island. The white marble of its hills is quarried nearby, and the town is known for its books.
gazetteer_edit.name: Baile Mòr dhomhain

gazetteer_edit.new: It is the market town of the east coast. The first glass-house on Rodos was built here and still works, and the town also makes cheese, boots and sail-cloth.
gazetteer_edit.name: Baile Mòr dhìreach

gazetteer_edit.new: Its own vineyards give the plain's wine, and the town salts meat, makes boots and dips candles.
gazetteer_edit.name: Baile Mòr fhionn

gazetteer_edit.new: Its market right is among the oldest on the island, and its own trade is in cheese, honey and garments.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cathair fhada

gazetteer_edit.new: It has been the market town of the north-west coast since the shires were drawn, and it sends fish, whale-oil, seal-oil, amber, dyes and tobacco south. Glass is blown from the white sand of its beaches.
gazetteer_edit.name: Ceann mhòr

gazetteer_edit.new: It is the market town of the north coast. Fish, whale-oil and wool come to its strand-market, and its whale-boats go out every summer.
gazetteer_edit.name: Àth fhionn

gazetteer_edit.new: Since the Severance it has been the market town of the north-western interior and the greatest cattle-market on Rodos. Its own trade is in paper and books.
gazetteer_edit.name: Muileann fhionn

gazetteer_edit.new: It sends the pearls of the south-eastern shallows and the clay of its fields to other markets.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cnoc bhàn

gazetteer_edit.new: It was chartered as the sixteenth market town after An Cogadh Fada, to victual the garrisons and the fleet.
gazetteer_edit.name: Caol ruadh

gazetteer_edit.new: Its yards are the largest shipyard on Rodos, and the town cuts the sails and makes the cheese of the east coast.
gazetteer_edit.name: Seann Dunn

gazetteer_edit.new: Its yards build seagoing hulls and cut their sails.
gazetteer_edit.name: Seann Dunn

gazetteer_edit.new: The fortress keeps its own boatyard and weaving-sheds, and its cheese goes down the river to Ros gheal.
gazetteer_edit.name: Inis ìseal

gazetteer_edit.new: Besides its pilgrims it lives on its shipyard, which builds seagoing hulls for the western coast, and on its cheese and books.
gazetteer_edit.name: Inis thais

gazetteer_edit.new: Its honey and its salted meat are sold in every market of the south, and its soap-boilers and weavers are the busiest in the gulf.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cathair mhòr

gazetteer_edit.new: The royal quays build seagoing hulls for the Crown.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cathair dhearg

gazetteer_edit.new: Its few townsmen boil soap and blow glass for the hill towns.
gazetteer_edit.name: Caol chrom

gazetteer_edit.new: Bog-iron is dug in the moss behind the town, and its forges have made arms and field-guns for the regiments since An Cogadh Fada.
gazetteer_edit.name: Àth naomh

gazetteer_edit.new: Its dyers make the reds and blues of the east, and it is one of the chief towns of the east for books and ink.
gazetteer_edit.name: Baile Mòr ruadh

gazetteer_edit.new: Its copyists and tailors work for the capital.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cuan uaine

gazetteer_edit.new: The customs town also boils soap and blows glass for the gulf.
gazetteer_edit.name: Ros bhàn

gazetteer_edit.new: Its forges are the chief armoury of the north-eastern hills.
gazetteer_edit.name: Baile Mòr uaine

gazetteer_edit.new: Its tailors and smiths work for the library's clerks and the hill towns, and its own woods give timber.
gazetteer_edit.name: Dùn thais

gazetteer_edit.new: The hemp for its yards grows in its own fields, and its copyists bind books for the south.
gazetteer_edit.name: Ceann mhin

gazetteer_edit.new: Its glass-house is the largest on the island.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cathair mhòr

gazetteer_edit.new: Its smiths make arms for the east coast.
gazetteer_edit.name: Muileann chiar

gazetteer_edit.new: The clay of its hill makes it the largest pottery on Rodos, and Cathair fhada sells its ware to the north.
gazetteer_edit.name: Dùn fhiadhaich

gazetteer_edit.new: Its clay-pits feed its potteries, and its soap-boilers serve the gulf.
gazetteer_edit.name: Ros dhìreach

gazetteer_edit.new: Its fields grow the dye-plants of the north-east, and its colours go to the feast-market at Seann Tarr.
gazetteer_edit.name: Baile fhiadhaich

gazetteer_edit.new: Its smiths make the tools of the north-west.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cathair gheal

gazetteer_edit.new: The charcoal-burners of its woods supply the forges of the gulf, and the town boils soap.
gazetteer_edit.name: Baile chrom

gazetteer_edit.new: Bog-iron dug behind the pans feeds its forges, which cast field-guns for the regiments.
gazetteer_edit.name: Caol ìseal

gazetteer_edit.new: Its dye-fields and smithies are the busiest in the Tuathaich north.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cnoc ghorm

gazetteer_edit.new: Gold is washed from the stream below the town, and its refiners make blanks for the mint.
gazetteer_edit.name: Baile dhìreach

gazetteer_edit.new: Charcoal-burning is the chief trade of its woods, and it binds books, a craft the Tuathaich learned at Muileann leathan.
gazetteer_edit.name: Àth fhada

gazetteer_edit.new: Charcoal from its woods and books copied in its hostels are its trades.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cathair naomh

gazetteer_edit.new: Charcoal-burners work the woods under its walls.
gazetteer_edit.name: Dùn dhubh

gazetteer_edit.new: Its people gather amber on the strands of the Hawk bay.
gazetteer_edit.name: Cill àrsaidh

gazetteer_edit.new: Amber washed up on the nearby shore is its other trade.
gazetteer_edit.name: Muileann leathan

gazetteer_edit.new: Furs and hides from the eastern hills are sold at its fair.
gazetteer_edit.name: Àth ruadh

gazetteer_edit.new: Glass is blown there from the white sand of its own shore.
gazetteer_edit.name: Seann Skell

gazetteer_edit.new: The white sand of its river banks goes to its glass-house.
gazetteer_edit.name: Inis mhòr

gazetteer_edit.new: The dark wine pressed on its slopes is sold along the eastern road.
gazetteer_edit.name: Àth shean

gazetteer_edit.new: Its scent-makers distil the best-known scent on the island.
gazetteer_edit.name: Seann Vell

gazetteer_edit.new: Its women distil scent-waters, the town's second trade after the fishing.
gazetteer_edit.name: Caol fhiadhaich

gazetteer_edit.new: Its salt-pans supply the whole eastern seaboard.
gazetteer_edit.name: Àth bheag

gazetteer_edit.new: Its salt-pans have sold salt since the first years of the humans' trade, and the olive-yard on its sheltered shore is the only one on the island.
gazetteer_edit.name: Seann Warr

gazetteer_edit.new: Copper is mined in the hills behind it, and the town's new street is named for the Sloc Mòr.
gazetteer_edit.name: Àth fhiadhaich

gazetteer_edit.new: Its paper-mill makes the paper of the royal chronicle.
gazetteer_edit.name: Tobar dhìreach

gazetteer_edit.new: Its wool mills, built with the Moot's money, make the grey twill of the north.
gazetteer_edit.name: Doire ghlas

gazetteer_edit.new: Its chartered weavers make cloth from southern wool.
gazetteer_edit.name: Baile chiar

gazetteer_edit.new: Paper has been made here since the Age of Sundering, and its copyists and binders work for the library.
gazetteer_edit.name: Muileann chaol

unsure: The present economy runs on dubhan (VI-0041, VI-0154) but the goods list has no dubhan. The nearest good is Oil (i35: fuel, 1 sea cell, recipes olives/whales, produced by no burg). It could be renamed 'Dubhan' and given to the dubhan works at the southern Seann Skell (burg 431, VI-0008, VI-0045) as a crafted good; left alone because its recipes (olive oil, whale oil) do not fit dubhan and whale-oil is written into the history as lamp oil.

Coins are crafted in 27 small burgs (Baile naomh 48, Doire dhearg 81, ... Baile dhìreach 384, Muileann gheal 288, Àth fhiadhaich 12). The history has one mint (Cathair dhearg, V-0024). Written in as coin-blanks refined for the mint (new V-0137a) rather than editing 27 burgs and their deals.

Ships are built at Ros fhionn (burg 76, port 0), whose harbour silted in III-0166. Written as river barges and hulls on its river; if that is not wanted, its Ships/Sails/Ropes production entries could be removed.

Muileann fhionn (160) is a market centre; its gazetteer says human-built fort and mill of the Age of Strangers, but IV-0288 (1920) calls it 'a Ròdaich mill town'. Not an economy question; flagged for the burg/gazetteer layer. New V-0044a follows the gazetteer.
Perfume (27 producers, the costliest good traded between markets) is kept and written in as scent-waters of bog-myrtle and meadowsweet (new V-0107a); renaming it was not needed.

The biome record labels 616 farmed land cells 'Glacier' and 567 'Tundra' although they grow grain, wood, hemp and honey (the goods were placed under other biome rules). The appendix describes these as 'the high bare north' and does not use the biome names; the biome layer may want to relabel them.

Section V of G_trade.md cites new events by {{date:...}} (VI-0131a, V-0036a, etc.); if an annals_add is not applied, the matching token in the appendix must be dropped too. Every new event id cited in G_trade.md: I-0116a, II-0064a, II-0106a, II-0134a, III-0070a, III-0088a, III-0119a, III-0126a, III-0135a, III-0156a, III-0168a, III-0181a, III-0214a, IV-0122a, IV-0127a, IV-0142a, V-0014a, V-0036a, V-0044a, V-0107a, V-0137a, VI-0120a, VI-0131a, VI-0132a.
Prices in the appendix are given in 'the realm-coin' (bonn-rìoghachd); the map's treasury/price units have no named denomination, and the history names none for the restored coinage.
